story.what_it_does: HUDCO is a government-owned lender that finances housing and urban infrastructure projects. Its loan book was about ₹1.6 lakh crore at 31 March 2026 and about ₹1.86 lakh crore by H1 FY27.
story.plans: Management targets a loan book of ₹3 lakh crore by 2030 and FY27 disbursements of about ₹65,000 crore. It also aims to meet RBI's NBFC-IFC conditions by March 2027, raise overseas borrowings under the RBI forex swap facility, and resolve remaining NCLT bad loans.
story.moat: Government ownership and a focus on housing and urban infrastructure give HUDCO a specialised lending niche, and its cost of funds of about 7% is low. Asset quality is very strong, with net NPA of 0.044% and provision coverage of about 94%. The notes do not describe any other formal competitive advantage.

scenarios.story: Loan book growth stays near 28-29% and bad loans stay very low, so profit keeps rising as it did in H1 FY27 (₹1,762 crore versus ₹1,340 crore). Falling borrowing costs and the planned ₹65,000 crore of disbursements help it move toward the 2030 target.
signals_to_watch: Loan book growth staying near 28-29% year on year

scenarios.story: The loan book keeps growing, but margins stay thin: net interest margin was 2.64% in H1 FY27, below the 3.1% outlook. Profit grows with the book, while FY26's profit jump was helped by one-off items.
signals_to_watch: Net interest margin and spread versus the 3% and 2% guidance
Progress on NBFC-IFC conditions and the RBI extension request

scenarios.story: Margins keep shrinking and leverage stays high (debt-equity 7.28 times at Dec-25). A higher share of foreign currency loans could add forex cost, and unresolved governance and RBI compliance issues could weigh on the company.
signals_to_watch: Debt-to-equity and interest coverage (7.28 times and 1.40 at Dec-25)
